text:
Passive movement is joint movement produced entirely by an external force, such as a therapist, a machine, or the patient's other limb, while the patient's muscles stay relaxed, so nothing resists the motion and it stops at the end of the available range. It is used to maintain range of motion and assess joint mobility, and it differs from active movement (the patient moves alone) and active-assisted movement (the patient contributes with help). Of the two options in the team note, the first ("movement without resistance, stopping at end of range") matches this; the second contradicts itself by saying "with resistance" and then "nothing resists the motion."

CONFIDENCE: 85
